summary: Close the deal, then close the consumption. Revenue only lands when usage ramps.

skills.label: Pricing unit fluency
skills.definition: Explain the pricing unit in the buyer’s workload terms, not the rate card.
skills.evidence: The buyer restates the cost in their own workload terms.

talk_track.move: Translate the unit into cost per piece of the buyer’s work.
talk_track.strong: At your volume, that is about this much per case and this much per month.
talk_track.weak: Pricing is per million tokens. I can share the rate card after this.
talk_track.proof: Buyer restates the cost in workload terms

rep.buyer_line: I do not understand how tokens turn into a monthly bill.
rep.off_move: Most customers find it lands below their current spend, so I would not worry about it yet.

replies.elite: That I can take to finance. Per case is how we budget anyway.
replies.weak: I cannot take a rate card to finance. I need it in terms of our work.
replies.trap: Not worrying is how bills surprise us. I need it in terms finance can check.

curveball.speaker: CFO
curveball.line: Usage pricing scares me. I cannot budget for a number that moves.
curveball.elite: Then let us fix it: at your volume, here is the monthly cost, with a ceiling we both agree.
curveball.weak: Most customers find it evens out over the year, so it is quite predictable.
curveball.trap: We can switch you to a flat license instead. It costs more, but it is fixed.

skills.label: Bounded proof of value
skills.definition: Agree scope, exit criteria and an end date before any pilot starts.
skills.evidence: Scope, exit criteria and end date are agreed before the pilot.

talk_track.move: Bound the pilot: one workload, a pass bar, and a stop date.
talk_track.strong: Four weeks, one workload, and we stop if accuracy is under 95 percent. Agreed?
talk_track.weak: Sure. We can start with a free pilot and expand scope as your team gets comfortable.
talk_track.proof: Buyer agrees scope, exit criteria and an end date

rep.buyer_line: Can we just pilot it for a while and see how it goes?
rep.off_move: Let us pilot it across all three teams at once, so you see the full value quickly.

replies.elite: Agreed. A fixed end date makes it easier to get the team's time.
replies.weak: Open-ended pilots drift here. We still have two running from last year.
replies.trap: Three teams at once is a rollout, not a pilot. Nobody will own the result.

curveball.speaker: VP Engineering
curveball.line: We want a three-month pilot across every use case before we commit.
curveball.elite: Let us make it four weeks on the use case with the clearest number, with a pass bar agreed now.
curveball.weak: Happy to support that. We can staff it so every team gets attention.
curveball.trap: Sure. We will waive the fee so there is no risk on your side.

skills.label: Ramp and commit design
skills.definition: Size the commit to the forecast, with on-demand headroom while usage proves out.
skills.evidence: The buyer accepts a ramp schedule and a commit level.

talk_track.move: Propose a commit below forecast and on-demand above it.
talk_track.strong: Commit to 60 percent of the forecast and run the rest on demand until usage proves out.
talk_track.weak: If you sign for the full forecast upfront, I can get you our best discount.
talk_track.pin: Can we ramp the commit in phases, so year-one volume matches real usage?
talk_track.settle: Let us figure out the commit size later.
talk_track.assume: Let us lock the biggest commit we can, so you get the best discount.

rep.buyer_line: Procurement will want to know exactly what we are signing up for in year one.
rep.off_move: Most customers sign a three-year deal, so procurement gets price certainty.

replies.weak: I need the commit sized to what we will actually use, not to the discount.
replies.trap: Three years on volume we have not seen yet is not certainty. It is risk.
replies.settle: Later is how we end up overcommitted. I would rather size it now.
replies.assume: We have been burned by that before. Shelfware is hard to explain.

curveball.speaker: Procurement
curveball.line: Give us your best price for a three-year, all-in commitment.
curveball.elite: I can, but I would rather you start lower and step up as usage proves out. Here is that shape.
curveball.weak: Here is the three-year number. It includes our biggest discount tier.
curveball.trap: If you sign by Friday, I can add another ten percent off.

skills.label: Usage forecast
skills.definition: Build the volume forecast from the buyer’s own workload numbers.
skills.evidence: The buyer supplies current volume, growth and seasonality.

talk_track.move: Ask for today’s volume, next year’s growth and the peaks.
talk_track.strong: How much volume do you handle a month today, and what do you expect next year?
talk_track.weak: Roughly what size is the team that would use this?
talk_track.pin: What does peak-season volume look like versus a normal month?
talk_track.settle: Okay, lots of volume. Got it.
talk_track.assume: I will assume you look like our average customer.

rep.buyer_line: Before we talk price, you should know our volumes are not small.
rep.off_move: No problem. I will size it on our typical customer profile and we can true up later.

replies.weak: Headcount will not tell you much. Our volume swings a lot through the year.
replies.trap: If you size this on a typical profile, the bill will surprise both of us.
replies.settle: Lots is not a forecast. I can get you real numbers if you ask for them.
replies.assume: We are not average. Our peaks would break that assumption.

curveball.speaker: CFO
curveball.line: Last year's AI vendor bill came in at triple the estimate. Explain why you are different.
curveball.elite: Only if we build the estimate together, from your monthly volume and your peaks. Can we do that now?
curveball.weak: Our estimates are usually within ten percent, so that should not happen.
curveball.trap: That vendor priced poorly. Our rates are much lower, so you are safe.

skills.label: Adoption plan
skills.definition: Plan who uses it, for what, and the usage target in the first 90 days.
skills.evidence: The buyer names users, use cases and a usage target.

talk_track.move: Name the first users and their week-one use case.
talk_track.strong: Who are the first 50 users, and what does week-one adoption look like for them?
talk_track.weak: Let me set up a refresher training session for the whole team.
talk_track.proof: Buyer names users and a usage target

rep.buyer_line: Usage is at 30 percent of what we forecast. What now?
rep.off_move: That is normal early on. Usage usually catches up by the second quarter.

replies.elite: The senior team leads would go first. Week one is a stretch, but we can name them.
replies.weak: Training everyone again will not fix it. People do not see why they should use it.
replies.trap: Waiting for it to catch up is what I have to explain upstairs.

curveball.speaker: COO
curveball.line: We signed. Now my managers say their teams have no time to learn a new tool.
curveball.elite: Then let us start with ten people whose week it saves most, and show the others their numbers.
curveball.weak: We have great training content. I will share the full library with every manager.
curveball.trap: Usage will grow once they see it. Most teams come around within a quarter.

skills.label: Cost-to-serve awareness
skills.definition: Trade, never give: any discount narrows scope so the unit cost still works.
skills.evidence: A concession is traded for something of equal value.

talk_track.move: Trade a concession for scope, term or volume.
talk_track.strong: If we discount, we narrow the scope, so the unit cost still works for both of us.
talk_track.weak: Let me see what I can do. I can probably get approval for 15 percent.
talk_track.proof: Buyer agrees a trade for any concession

rep.buyer_line: Your price is 20 percent higher than the other vendor.
rep.off_move: If that is what it takes, I will match their price to get this done.

replies.elite: That is reasonable. Show me the narrower scope and I will compare like for like.
replies.weak: That was quick. It makes me wonder what the original price was based on.
replies.trap: If you can match it that easily, I am not sure what I was paying for.

curveball.speaker: Procurement
curveball.line: Take twenty percent off or we walk.
curveball.elite: I can move on price if we move on something else. Would a longer term or narrower scope work?
curveball.weak: Twenty is hard. Let me see if I can get you twelve.
curveball.trap: Understood. I will get you the twenty so we can close this week.
